To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetic field can play an important role in the dynamical evolution of elephant trunks.
the formation of elephant trunks can be affected by the presence of a magnetic field, and that the evolution of these structures can be significantly affected by the magnetic field strength.

(1) the magnetic field is swept into the direction of the radiation propagation by the dynamical evolution of the pillars; (2) this effect is significantly enhanced in the presence of weaker magnetic fields; (3) the magnetic field can prevent the evolution of pillars to cometary structures, and (4) in the absence of additional sources of dense material, the pillars evolve to cometary globules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of elephant trunks, which are pillars of dense gas formed at the boundaries of expanding ionised regions.
the effects of the radiation and magnetic field on the formation of the pillars of dense gas in HII regions, and on the subsequent evolution of these structures.
the role of magnetic fields in the formation and evolution, and the stability, of pillars and globules in star-forming regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
magnetic fields can play a key role in the evolution of pillars and cometary globules, but only if they are of sufficient strength and orientation.

the magnetic fields of the order of 10μG, which is a typical value for the diffuse ISM, are sufficient to explain the alignment of pillars and globules in the presence of the ionising radiation, and that the fields in the range from'10 to'100μG are able to explain the observed morphology of the pillars and globules.
